day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00. Use the morning to rest on the plane and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00. Take the 747 express bus (~$11 CAD) to downtown, then connect to Old Montreal. Check in to your accommodation, freshen up, and take a leisurely self-guided walk through the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal to get your bearings. Stroll along Rue Saint-Paul, admire the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior (free from outside), and soak in the historic architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Old Montreal Food Crawl – Begin your Montreal food journey right in your neighbourhood. Stop at Olive et Gourmando for a famous sandwich or pastry, grab a poutine from a local counter like La Banquise's Old Montreal outpost, and finish with a soft-serve from a nearby crêperie. The warm summer evening (~25°C) makes wandering the lit cobblestone streets magical.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport or on arrival – a bagel or sandwich from a terminal café (~$10–12 CAD)
meals.dinner: Old Montreal Food Crawl stops: Olive et Gourmando for a sandwich (~$14 CAD), followed by a classic poutine at a local counter (~$12 CAD). Budget ~$25–30 CAD total.

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a OPUS card at the airport or metro station for unlimited transit use (~$10 CAD/day or pay-per-ride). Old Montreal is very walkable from most accommodations in the area. Keep luggage light for the bus ride in.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour – Take the metro (Orange Line) north to Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest open-air markets. Spend 2–3 hours sampling Quebec cheeses, fresh maple products, local fruits, artisan breads, and charcuterie from vendor stalls. Many vendors offer free tastings. Stock up on affordable snacks and picnic supplies for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, head to Parc La Fontaine (a short metro/bus ride away) for a relaxed budget-friendly picnic with your market finds. Enjoy the park's fountains and green space. Afterward, explore the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood on foot – browse the colourful duplexes, murals, and independent boutiques along Avenue du Mont-Royal.
day_by_day.evening: St-Laurent Boulevard Festival Strip – Head to the legendary 'Main' (Boulevard Saint-Laurent) to experience Montreal's vibrant summer festival scene. In mid-July, festivals like the Montreal International Jazz Festival or Just for Laughs street events may have free outdoor stages. Stroll the strip, enjoy free live performances, and grab affordable street food from festival vendors.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh Montreal-style bagel from a local café near your Old Montreal accommodation (~$3–5 CAD) with coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic assembled from Jean-Talon Market – cheese, bread, fruit, and a local pastry (~$12–15 CAD total)
meals.dinner: Festival street food on St-Laurent – try a smoked meat sandwich from a nearby deli like Schwartz's (~$12 CAD) or grab tacos/crepes from a festival stall (~$10–14 CAD). Budget ~$12–15 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is open daily and is most lively in the morning. Bring a reusable bag for market purchases. Check the Montreal en Fête or Tourism Montreal website for exact festival schedules on St-Laurent this week – many events are free or have free zones.

day_by_day.morning: Hike or bike up Mont Royal Park – rent a BIXI bike (~$7 CAD for a single trip or $15/day pass) and cycle from Old Montreal up to Parc du Mont-Royal. Hike the Olmsted Trail to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for a stunning panoramic view of the city skyline. The park is free to enter and a beloved local experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the mountain and explore Mile End neighbourhood, known for its bohemian vibe and incredible food culture. Visit Fairmount Bagel or St-Viateur Bagel (both legendary and under $2/bagel) and browse the street art and murals. Walk along Avenue Bernard for a taste of local neighbourhood life.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (summer edition events or related gastronomy events) – Check if any affiliated summer food or cultural events are running this week. If not, head to a local BYOB (apportez votre vin) restaurant, a uniquely Montreal dining tradition. Many BYOBs in the Plateau or Mile End offer gourmet meals at very affordable prices since you bring your own wine from a nearby SAQ (liquor store).

meals.breakfast: Fresh bagel from Fairmount or St-Viateur in Mile End (~$2–4 CAD) with cream cheese
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch at a Mile End café or grab a falafel wrap from a local Middle Eastern spot on Avenue du Parc (~$10–12 CAD)
meals.dinner: BYOB restaurant in the Plateau – look for set menus or table d'hôte options (~$20–28 CAD per person for a full meal). Pick up a bottle of wine at SAQ beforehand (~$13–15 CAD) to keep costs low.

day_by_day.notes: BIXI bike stations are located throughout Old Montreal and the city – the app makes it easy to find docking stations. Mont Royal Park can get busy on summer weekends; go early for a quieter experience. BYOB restaurants are a quintessential Montreal budget hack – search 'BYOB Montreal Plateau' for top-rated affordable options.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Latin Quarter (Quartier Latin) and Village neighbourhoods on foot. Visit Square Saint-Louis, a beautiful Victorian square popular with locals. Browse the used bookshops and vintage stores along Rue Saint-Denis for unique, affordable souvenirs. On summer Saturdays, local street markets and pop-ups often appear along this stretch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Old Montreal for a final afternoon in your home neighbourhood. Visit the Pointe-à-Callière Museum exterior and the Old Port waterfront (free to walk). Rent a paddleboat or simply relax along the St. Lawrence River waterfront. If time allows, pop into the Bonsecours Market (free entry) to browse local artisan goods and pick up last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner celebration on a budget – head to Chinatown (a short walk from Old Montreal) for an incredibly affordable and delicious farewell meal. Chinatown restaurants offer generous portions of Vietnamese pho, Chinese dim sum, or Szechuan dishes for $10–15 CAD. Afterward, take one last evening stroll along Rue Saint-Paul to soak in the atmosphere of Old Montreal lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near your hotel – croissant and café au lait from a local Old Montreal boulangerie (~$7–9 CAD)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap lunch from a food truck or dépanneur (corner store) near the Old Port (~$8–10 CAD) – Montreal has excellent food trucks in summer
meals.dinner: Chinatown farewell dinner – pho, dim sum, or noodle dish at a local restaurant (~$12–15 CAD per person). Budget-friendly and delicious.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 – store luggage at your accommodation or a nearby luggage storage service if your departure is later. The Old Port waterfront is free and beautiful on a warm summer evening. Saturday in Montreal is lively with street performers, markets, and festivals – keep an eye out for spontaneous free events throughout the day.

The crawl is walkable directly from the hotel.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or on arrival; alternatively pick up a sandwich and pastry at Olive et Gourmando during the afternoon food crawl (~$15–20 CAD).
meals.dinner: Garde Manger (Old Montreal) — a beloved mid-range bistro known for creative Quebec-inspired dishes and a lively atmosphere. Budget ~$40–55 CAD per person with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. The Old Montreal Food Crawl is self-paced and perfect for easing into the city. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the cobblestones. Check hotel concierge for any same-week festival schedules on St-Laurent.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Bagel and Smoked Meat Breakfast: Take the Metro (Orange Line, ~15 min) up to the Mile End neighbourhood. Start at the legendary St-Viateur Bagel shop for fresh wood-fired Montreal-style bagels, then walk over to Schwartz's Deli or Beauty's Luncheonette for a classic smoked meat breakfast experience. Explore the eclectic Mile End murals and indie boutiques afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Head north to Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh fruit, charcuterie, and local specialties from market vendors. Pick up picnic supplies if desired. The market is vibrant in summer and a true local experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the St-Laurent Boulevard Festival Strip for the evening peak hours. In mid-July, the Montreal International Jazz Festival or other summer street festivals are typically in full swing nearby. Enjoy live performances, food stalls, and the electric atmosphere of Montreal in summer.

meals.breakfast: St-Viateur Bagel (fresh bagels with cream cheese or smoked salmon, ~$8–12 CAD) followed by smoked meat at Schwartz's Deli (~$18–25 CAD).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch assembled from Jean-Talon Market vendors — Quebec cheese, charcuterie, fresh bread, and seasonal fruit (~$20–30 CAD total).
meals.dinner: Dine at a restaurant along St-Laurent Boulevard during the festival strip — try Brasserie T! or Moishes Steakhouse for a mid-range sit-down meal (~$40–55 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is best visited before 2 PM on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Bring a reusable bag for market finds. The Metro Laurier or Jean-Talon stations are convenient. Check the official Montreal festivals website (mtl.org) for exact festival schedules and free concert lineups on St-Laurent.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood on foot — browse independent cafés, colourful staircases, and local boutiques. Stop for a leisurely coffee and pastry at Café Olimpico or Café Névé, both neighbourhood institutions beloved by locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Montreal Botanical Garden and nearby Parc Maisonneuve for a relaxed outdoor afternoon. The gardens are stunning in July with summer blooms. Alternatively, if a major festival is running downtown (e.g., Just for Laughs / Juste pour rire, typically mid-July), spend the afternoon catching free outdoor shows and roaming the festival village around Rue Saint-Denis.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (summer edition events or equivalent summer gastronomy event): Check for any special ticketed gastronomy dinners, pop-up chef events, or performing arts shows happening this week. Montreal's festival calendar in July is packed — book a ticketed evening experience or a chef's tasting menu at a celebrated restaurant for a special night out.

meals.breakfast: Café Olimpico or Café Névé in Plateau-Mont-Royal — espresso, croissant or avocado toast (~$12–18 CAD).
meals.lunch: Fabergé or L'Express on Rue Saint-Denis — classic French-Quebec bistro fare in a neighbourhood setting (~$25–35 CAD).
meals.dinner: Joe Beef or Liverpool House (Little Burgundy) — iconic Montreal dining institutions with a focus on indulgent Quebec cuisine. Reserve in advance. Budget ~$65–85 CAD per person for a special evening.

day_by_day.notes: Friday evening is lively across Montreal — book dinner reservations at Joe Beef or Liverpool House well in advance as they fill up quickly. If budget is a concern for dinner, Satay Brothers nearby is an excellent, more affordable alternative (~$25–35 CAD). Check mtl.org for any free Just for Laughs outdoor shows running this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Old Montreal for a relaxed final morning — visit the Notre-Dame Basilica (book a timed entry ticket online, ~$15 CAD) to admire the stunning interior. Afterward, browse the artisan stalls at the Old Port weekend market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final neighbourhood wander: Walk or bike along the Lachine Canal path, a beloved local green corridor connecting Old Montreal to the Saint-Henri and Little Burgundy neighbourhoods. Rent a BIXI bike (~$6–10 CAD for a day pass) and enjoy the flat, scenic ride. Stop at Atwater Market along the canal for one last taste of local Quebec products and a final souvenir shop.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner back in Old Montreal within walking distance of the hotel. Enjoy a relaxed last meal celebrating the trip before packing up.

meals.breakfast: Café in Old Montreal — try Crew Collective & Café (stunning bank-turned-café) for coffee and a pastry (~$10–15 CAD).
meals.lunch: Atwater Market food stalls — grab a gourmet sandwich, Quebec cheese board, or a crepe from a market vendor along the Lachine Canal (~$15–25 CAD).
meals.dinner: Holder Restaurant (Old Montreal) — reliable mid-range brasserie with excellent French-Quebec cuisine, great for a relaxed farewell dinner within walking distance of the hotel (~$40–55 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: BIXI bikes are available at numerous docking stations throughout Old Montreal and along the canal — the Lachine Canal path is flat and beginner-friendly. Book Notre-Dame Basilica tickets online in advance to skip the queue. If departing early the next morning, pack bags the night before and confirm checkout time with the hotel. Saturday markets at both Old Port and Atwater are at their best in summer — arrive by 10 AM for the freshest selection.

day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Food Crawl — Begin your Montreal experience with a leisurely stroll through the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal. Stop at the iconic Olive et Gourmando for artisanal pastries and a light bite, then explore Marché Bonsecours and the surrounding historic architecture. Pop into curated local shops for Quebec artisan products and maple treats to get a feel for the city's culinary identity.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Toqué! — One of Montreal's most celebrated fine-dining institutions, Toqué! on Place Jean-Paul-Riopelle offers an exquisite tasting menu driven by Quebec terroir. Expect expertly crafted dishes featuring local produce, foie gras, and seasonal ingredients paired with an exceptional wine list. Reserve the chef's tasting menu for the full luxury experience.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal prior to landing.
meals.lunch: Light welcome bite at Olive et Gourmando in Old Montreal — artisan sandwiches, fresh-baked pastries, and specialty coffee in a charming rustic setting.
meals.dinner: Toqué! — Quebec-driven fine-dining tasting menu with wine pairing. One of Canada's most acclaimed restaurants, steps from your hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer recommended for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm hotel early check-in in advance. Old Montreal is extremely walkable from your accommodation — no car needed for the afternoon crawl. Make Toqué! reservations well in advance as it books out quickly in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Bagel and Smoked Meat Breakfast — Head north to the beloved Mile End neighbourhood for an iconic Montreal morning. Begin at St-Viateur Bagel for freshly wood-fired sesame bagels, warm from the oven. Then walk to Schwartz's Deli for a classic smoked meat sandwich — a Montreal institution. Soak in the eclectic, artistic energy of this culturally rich district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour — Continue deeper into the Plateau and Little Italy to explore Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest and most vibrant open-air markets. Join a premium guided food tour sampling Quebec cheeses, artisan charcuterie, fresh maple products, heirloom vegetables, and local fruit. Engage with passionate producers and discover the depth of Quebec's culinary heritage.
day_by_day.evening: St-Laurent Boulevard Festival Strip — Return to the legendary 'Main' (Boulevard St-Laurent) as the city comes alive with summer festival energy. Stroll the vibrant strip during one of Montreal's many summer street festivals — expect live music, street performers, local artisan vendors, and an electric atmosphere. Cap the night with cocktails and dinner at a premium resto-bar along the strip.

meals.breakfast: St-Viateur Bagel (Mile End) — wood-fired Montreal bagels with cream cheese and smoked salmon, paired with coffee from a nearby specialty café such as Café Olimpico.
meals.lunch: Jean-Talon Market tastings during the food tour — curated samplings of Quebec cheeses, charcuterie, maple treats, and seasonal produce included in the tour experience.
meals.dinner: Milos Montreal (Avenue du Parc) — a world-renowned Greek seafood restaurant beloved by Montreal's elite. Whole fresh fish, premium mezze, and an outstanding wine list in an elegant yet convivial setting.

day_by_day.notes: The Jean-Talon Market food tour should be pre-booked with a premium culinary tour operator such as Fitz & Follwell or a private guide. Wear comfortable shoes for a full day of walking between neighbourhoods. A taxi or rideshare between Mile End and Jean-Talon takes under 10 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Mount Royal Park Morning Hike & Scenic Overlook — Begin the day with an invigorating walk up Mont Royal, the forested hill at the heart of the city. Hire a private guide or explore independently via the Kondiaronk Belvedere trail for sweeping panoramic views of the Montreal skyline and the St. Lawrence River. The park is lush and green in July — ideal for a premium outdoor morning experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighbourhood Exploration & Spa Retreat — Descend into the charming Plateau neighbourhood for a leisurely afternoon. Browse independent boutiques, galleries, and design shops along Laurier Avenue and Duluth Street. Then indulge in a 90-minute treatment at Scandinave Spa Old Montreal or Bota Bota Spa (a converted riverboat spa on the Old Port) — both offer world-class thermal spa circuits perfectly suited to a luxury itinerary.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (Special Summer Edition) — Immerse yourself in Montreal's celebrated festival culture. In summer, the city hosts a rich calendar of gastronomy and performing arts events. Attend a curated festival dinner, rooftop concert, or chef's collaborative dinner event tied to the city's summer programming. Check the festival calendar for July 2027 for ticketed premium experiences such as grand chef dinners or exclusive tasting events.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or brunch at Maison Boulud (Ritz-Carlton Montreal) — a luxurious French-inspired brunch by celebrated chef Daniel Boulud, featuring eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, viennoiseries, and fresh-pressed juices in an opulent setting.
meals.lunch: L'Express (Plateau-Mont-Royal) — a beloved Montreal bistro institution with steak tartare, duck confit, and an exceptional French wine list in a classic Parisian brasserie atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Festival grand chef dinner or, alternatively, Le Mousso — one of Montreal's most innovative and lauded fine-dining experiences offering a bold, creative tasting menu in an intimate setting. Reserve the full tasting menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Bota Bota Spa is located in the Old Port, very close to your hotel — ideal for the afternoon. Book spa treatments and festival dinners well in advance as July is peak season. The Mont Royal hike is approximately 2–3 hours at a relaxed pace and is best enjoyed before 10:00 AM to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Old Port & Waterfront Morning Stroll — Enjoy a final leisurely morning exploring the Old Port waterfront promenade, just steps from your hotel. Visit the Pointe-à-Callière Museum of Archaeology for a premium cultural experience exploring Montreal's founding history. The museum sits atop actual archaeological ruins of the original city — a fascinating and unique attraction.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell Gourmet Shopping & Culinary Souvenirs — Spend your final afternoon curating luxury Quebec souvenirs. Visit the boutiques of Old Montreal for artisan maple products, Quebec ice ciders, local cheeses to travel with, and handcrafted gifts. Stop at Épicerie Européenne or a specialty food shop for premium Quebec pantry items. Enjoy a final afternoon coffee and pastry at a terrace café overlooking Place Jacques-Cartier.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner at Le Filet or Maison Boulud — Choose between Le Filet, an intimate and elegant seafood-focused restaurant beloved by Montreal's food cognoscenti, or return to Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton for a grand farewell dinner in one of the city's most prestigious dining rooms. Toast to an extraordinary Montreal experience with a bottle of fine Quebec or French wine.

meals.breakfast: Hôtel Gault or your hotel's breakfast service — a relaxed, unhurried luxury breakfast with fresh pastries, local yogurt, fruit, and specialty coffee to ease into the final day.
meals.lunch: Terrasse Place d'Armes or a sunny terrace restaurant on Place Jacques-Cartier — classic Quebec poutine elevated with duck confit and truffle, lobster bisque, or a charcuterie board with local Quebec products.
meals.dinner: Le Filet (Mile End) — acclaimed for its refined, ingredient-forward seafood dishes and outstanding natural wine list. Intimate, elegant, and the perfect send-off for a luxury Montreal trip. Alternatively, Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton for grand French-inspired cuisine in a legendary setting.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is later in the day. The Old Port is entirely walkable from your Old Montreal hotel — savour the final morning on foot. Consider purchasing Quebec ice cider (cidre de glace) or artisan maple butter as premium take-home gifts — both travel well and are uniquely Quebecois.
